name: Art trivia (medium)
description: 50 medium questions about visual art: painters, sculptors, famous works, movements, techniques, museums. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which Louvre employee stole the Mona Lisa in August 1911?
items.explain: Vincenzo Peruggia, a worker at the Louvre, stole the Mona Lisa on 21 August 1911.

source.title: Masterpiece Story: Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci

items.question: Which technique, a smoky haziness that softens outlines, is Leonardo da Vinci known for in the Mona Lisa?
items.explain: Leonardo used sfumato, a smoky haziness, to soften outlines and create an atmospheric effect around the figure.

source.title: Mona Lisa (article) - Khan Academy

items.question: Which French king acquired the Mona Lisa after Leonardo da Vinci's death in 1519?
items.explain: King Francis I of France acquired the painting after Leonardo died, and it later became the property of the French Republic.

source.title: Mona Lisa - Wikipedia

items.question: The Mona Lisa is also known as La Gioconda. Where does that name come from?
answers: The street in Florence where Leonardo worked
The family name of the sitter's husband
A nickname coined by King Francis I
The name of Leonardo's wealthy patron
items.correct: The family name of the sitter's husband
items.explain: According to Vasari, the sitter married a Florentine named del Giocondo, which gave the painting its other name.

source.title: Mona Lisa (La Gioconda) by LEONARDO da Vinci - Web Gallery of Art

items.question: Which critic's satirical 1874 review gave Impressionism its name?
items.explain: Louis Leroy mocked Monet's Impression, Sunrise in a review in Le Charivari and coined the term 'Impressionism'.

source.title: Impressionism - Wikipedia

items.question: Which Paris museum holds Monet's Impression, Sunrise, the painting that gave Impressionism its name?
items.explain: Impression, Sunrise is one of the best-known works in the Musée Marmottan Monet, which holds more than three hundred Impressionist and post-Impressionist paintings.

source.title: Musée Marmottan Monet - Wikipedia

items.question: Which French port does Monet's Impression, Sunrise depict?
items.explain: Monet painted the harbor of Le Havre, working from a window overlooking the port.

source.title: Impression, Sunrise - Britannica

items.question: The independent 1874 exhibition where Impression, Sunrise was first shown was an alternative to which official institution?
items.explain: The artists' own show was organized as an alternative to the traditional, state-run Salon.

source.title: Impression, Sunrise - Britannica

items.question: Which pope commissioned Michelangelo to paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
items.explain: The ceiling was painted between 1508 and 1512 at the commission of Pope Julius II.

source.title: Sistine Chapel ceiling - EPFL Graph Search

items.question: Which technique, applying water-mixed pigment to wet lime plaster, did Michelangelo use for the Sistine Chapel ceiling?
items.explain: The ceiling was painted as a fresco, which means applying pigment mixed with water to wet lime plaster.

source.title: Sistine Chapel Ceiling Painting by Michelangelo - Art in Context

items.question: After finishing the ceiling, Michelangelo returned to the Sistine Chapel to paint which large fresco behind the altar?
items.explain: Michelangelo came back to the chapel to create The Last Judgment, a large wall fresco behind the altar.

source.title: Sistine Chapel ceiling - Wikipedia

items.question: The nine central scenes of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, including The Creation of Adam, come from which book of the Bible?
items.explain: Central to the ceiling decoration are nine scenes from the Book of Genesis.

source.title: Sistine Chapel ceiling - EPFL Graph Search

items.question: After Michelangelo finished the ceiling, which artist created a set of large tapestries (1515–1516) to cover the lower walls of the Sistine Chapel?
items.explain: Raphael created the set of large tapestries in 1515–1516 for the lower part of the chapel walls.

source.title: Sistine Chapel ceiling - EPFL Graph Search

items.question: Which artist co-invented Cubism with Pablo Picasso in the first decade of the twentieth century?
items.explain: MoMA says Picasso invented Cubism with his close friend and collaborator Georges Braque.

source.title: Pablo Picasso. Les Demoiselles d'Avignon. Paris, June-July 1907 - MoMA

items.question: The 'Avignon' in Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon refers to a street in which city?
items.explain: The title refers to the carrer d'Avinyó (Avignon Street) in Barcelona, the city where Picasso spent his youth.

source.title: Pablo Picasso. Les Demoiselles d'Avignon. Paris, June-July 1907 - MoMA

items.question: The stylized features of the two rightmost figures in Les Demoiselles d'Avignon show Picasso's interest in what?
items.explain: MoMA notes that these figures reflect the formal innovations of African masks and sculpture, which Picasso and his peers collected.

source.title: Pablo Picasso. Les Demoiselles d'Avignon. Paris, June-July 1907 - MoMA

items.question: Which dealer showed Braque's work at his gallery on the rue Vignon in November 1908, introducing Cubism to the public?
items.explain: Cubism reached the public through Braque's one-man show at Daniel-Henry Kahnweiler's gallery, and Kahnweiler was a major supporter of Picasso and Braque.

source.title: Cubism Movement Overview - The Art Story

items.question: Which name is given to the phase of Cubism (c. 1912–1914) that followed Analytical Cubism?
items.explain: Picasso's Analytical Cubism (c. 1909–12) was followed by Synthetic Cubism (1912–14).

source.title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, Picasso: Analysis

items.question: In which French town did Vincent van Gogh paint The Starry Night while staying at an asylum?
items.explain: Van Gogh painted it in June 1889 at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy, inspired by the view from his window.

source.title: Vincent van Gogh. The Starry Night. Saint Rémy, June 1889 - MoMA

items.question: Which New York museum has held Van Gogh's The Starry Night since 1941?
answers: The Whitney Museum of American Art
items.explain: The Starry Night entered the permanent collection of the Museum of Modern Art in 1941.

source.title: Vincent van Gogh The Starry Night - The Museum of Modern Art

items.question: According to MoMA, which planet appears at center left in the night sky of The Starry Night, alongside the bright moon?
items.explain: MoMA describes the sky as dominated by the bright moon at right and Venus at center left.

source.title: Vincent van Gogh. The Starry Night. Saint Rémy, June 1889 - MoMA

items.question: Which technique, in which paint is laid on thickly so brushstrokes stand out, did van Gogh use in The Starry Night?
items.explain: Britannica notes that van Gogh used thick impasto and intense colors, applying paint directly to the canvas.

source.title: The Starry Night - Britannica

items.question: Rodin's The Thinker began as a figure for The Gates of Hell, which was inspired by an epic poem by which poet?
items.explain: The Gates of Hell drew on Dante's Divine Comedy, and the figure was first meant to represent Dante pondering his poem.

source.title: Auguste Rodin, The Thinker - Philadelphia Museum of Art

items.question: What was Rodin's The Thinker originally called?
items.explain: The Thinker was originally called The Poet and was conceived as part of The Gates of Hell.

source.title: The Thinker - Britannica

items.question: Rodin's Gates of Hell was commissioned in 1880 as bronze doors for a planned museum of what?
items.explain: The Gates of Hell was meant for a museum of decorative arts in Paris, which was never built.

source.title: The Thinker (Le Penseur) by Auguste Rodin - National Gallery of Art

items.question: When asked whether his soft watches were inspired by relativity, Dalí said they came from what?
answers: A candle melting in a church
A Camembert melting in the sun
A wilted flower in a vase
A clock left out in the rain
items.correct: A Camembert melting in the sun
items.explain: Dalí told Ilya Prigogine the soft watches were inspired by the Surrealist perception of a Camembert melting in the sun, not by the theory of relativity.

source.title: The Persistence of Memory, 1931 - Salvador Dali - WikiArt.org

items.question: Which Spanish artist helped Dalí meet members of the Surrealist group, which he joined in 1929?
items.explain: Dalí joined the Surrealists in 1929 after meeting some members of the group thanks to Joan Miró.

source.title: The Persistence of Memory: Understanding Dalí's Masterpiece - Artsper Magazine

items.question: Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring is not a portrait but which type of Dutch picture, meaning a 'head' of a character or type?
items.explain: A tronie is the Dutch 17th-century term for a head that was not meant to be a portrait of a specific person.

source.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring - Britannica

items.question: In which city is the Mauritshuis, the museum that owns Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring?
items.explain: The painting has been in the collection of the Mauritshuis in The Hague since 1902.

source.title: The Girl with a Pearl Earring, c.1665 - Johannes Vermeer - WikiArt.org

items.question: Which of these paintings is by Johannes Vermeer?
items.explain: Besides Girl with a Pearl Earring, Vermeer is known for The Milkmaid and View of Delft.

source.title: Vermeer's 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' is coming to Osaka - Time Out

items.question: In Botticelli's The Birth of Venus, the goddess arrives on the shore of which island?
items.explain: The Uffizi says the painting shows Venus arriving on the island of Cyprus, born of the sea spray and blown there by the winds.

source.title: The birth of Venus by Botticelli - Uffizi Galleries

items.question: What medium did Botticelli use for The Birth of Venus, according to the Uffizi?
items.explain: The Uffizi lists the technique of The Birth of Venus as tempera on canvas.

source.title: The birth of Venus by Botticelli - Uffizi Galleries

items.question: Which other large mythological painting by Botticelli hangs in the Uffizi alongside The Birth of Venus?
items.explain: Primavera is a large tempera painting by Botticelli in the Uffizi, often discussed alongside The Birth of Venus.

source.title: Primavera (Botticelli) - Wikipedia

items.question: In 1945 Jackson Pollock moved to Springs, New York, with his wife, which American painter?
items.explain: Pollock and his wife, the painter Lee Krasner, moved to Springs in 1945, and he developed his drip technique in the barn studio there.

source.title: Jackson Pollock - WikiArt.org

items.question: Which magazine gave Jackson Pollock the nickname 'Jack the Dripper' in 1956?
items.explain: In 1956 Time magazine called Pollock 'Jack the Dripper', a reference to his drip style of action painting.

source.title: Jackson Pollock - WikiArt.org

items.question: Which Regionalist painter taught Jackson Pollock before he moved to abstraction?
items.explain: Pollock trained under Thomas Hart Benton before abandoning established methods to experiment with abstract expressionism.

source.title: Jackson Pollock - A Look at the Famous Master of the Drip Painting - Art in Context

items.question: How many canvases made up Andy Warhol's original Campbell's Soup Cans, one for each soup variety then sold?
items.explain: MoMA says Warhol's first Campbell's Soup Cans series had thirty-two canvases, matching the number of soup varieties Campbell's then sold.

source.title: Andy Warhol. Campbell's Soup Cans. 1962 - MoMA

items.question: In which city did Warhol first exhibit Campbell's Soup Cans at the Ferus Gallery in July 1962?
items.explain: MoMA records that in July 1962 Warhol exhibited his Campbell's Soup Cans at the Ferus Gallery in Los Angeles.

source.title: Andy Warhol. Campbell's Soup Cans. 1962 - MoMA

items.question: After his Campbell's Soup Can paintings, Warhol shifted to which printing method, which gave more mechanical-looking results?
items.explain: After the soup can paintings, Warhol moved to silkscreen printing, which let him make multiple versions of one artwork.

source.title: Andy Warhol's Soup Cans: A Complete Guide to Pop Art Icon

items.question: Which museum owns Georges Seurat's A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884?
items.explain: The Art Institute of Chicago holds the nearly ten-foot-wide painting.

source.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884 - Art Institute of Chicago

items.question: Seurat's A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte initiated which art movement?
items.explain: The 1884–1886 painting altered the direction of modern art by initiating Neo-Impressionism.

source.title: Georges Seurat - Wikipedia

items.question: Which painter was strongly influenced by Seurat's pointillism and went on to paint in the same idiom?
items.explain: Seurat's ideas on pointillism had an especially strong influence on Paul Signac, who then painted in the same idiom.

source.title: Georges Seurat - Wikipedia

items.question: In which 1980s comedy does Cameron Frye stare intently at Seurat's La Grande Jatte during a scene at an art museum?
items.explain: The Art Institute of Chicago notes that Ferris's best friend Cameron Frye studies the painting in Ferris Bueller's Day Off.

source.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884 - Art Institute of Chicago

items.question: Rembrandt's The Night Watch actually shows a daytime scene. Why does 'night' appear in its title?
answers: The militia was assigned to guard the city after dark
Rembrandt painted it only by lamplight at night
A later owner commissioned it for his bedroom
Old darkened varnish made the scene look like night
items.correct: Old darkened varnish made the scene look like night
items.explain: The title is a later misidentification caused by centuries of darkened varnish, even though the scene takes place in daylight.

source.title: The Night Watch by Rembrandt van Rijn: Where to See It

items.question: Rembrandt's The Night Watch is a group portrait of what?
items.explain: The painting shows armed militiamen led by Captain Frans Banninck Cocq, assembled as a civic guard company.

source.title: The Night Watch - Britannica

items.question: Which Mexican muralist was the husband of Frida Kahlo, who lived with her at the Casa Azul?
items.explain: The Frida Kahlo Museum shows photos of Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera as a couple in the Casa Azul, which holds paintings by both artists.

source.title: Museum - Museo Frida Kahlo

items.question: In which year was Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul inaugurated as a museum?
items.explain: The museum's own site says the Casa Azul and its gardens have displayed personal objects and paintings since its inauguration in July 1958.

source.title: Museum - Museo Frida Kahlo

items.question: Edvard Munch's The Scream belongs to which semi-autobiographical cycle of works?
items.explain: The Scream was conceived as part of Munch's semi-autobiographical cycle 'The Frieze of Life'.

source.title: Edvard Munch, The Scream - Smarthistory

items.question: Munch's work, including The Scream, had a formative influence on which art movement?
items.explain: Munch's work, including The Scream, had a formative influence on the Expressionist movement.

source.title: The Scream - Wikipedia

items.question: Some scholars link the blood-red sky in The Scream to the 1883 eruption of which volcano?
items.explain: Some scholars think Munch was describing the sunsets tinted red by the 1883 Krakatoa eruption, about a decade before he painted The Scream.

source.title: The Scream - Wikipedia
